title: High-resolution ALMA Observations of Richly Structured Protoplanetary Disks in σ Orionis
question: Do millimeter continuum substructures (gaps, rings) form and survive in disks exposed to intermediate external UV radiation in sigma Orionis, and how do disk sizes compare to nearby regions?

what.value: Host star spectral type, mass, luminosity and external FUV field values

evidence.quote: Spectral type, stellar mass, stellar luminosity, and external FUV radiation field values come from (cite: 2023AA...679A..82M).
the median *Gaia* distance to members of $\sigma$ Orionis is 402 pc

what.value: Planet-mass fitting relations and hydrodynamical grid

evidence.quote: We use the fitting relations introduced in (cite: 2018ApJ...869L..47Z), which are implemented in code presented in (cite: 2022MNRAS.510.4473Z).

recipe.method: Flag CO channels in archival short-baseline data, self-calibrate, align EBs, combine with long-baseline data, image with multi-scale CLEAN and primary-beam correct

recipe.goal: Fit parametric radial intensity profiles in uv plane
recipe.method: Sum of central Gaussian plus N Gaussian rings, thin disk (flared surface for SO 897), model visibilities compared with weight-rescaled data
key_parameters: Adam optimizer, learning rate 0.02, 15,000 iterations; 2000 posterior samples
assumptions: Geometrically thin disk (flared surface for SO 897); posterior approximated as multivariate normal

recipe.goal: Identify substructures and measure location, width, depth
recipe.method: Rings = local maxima, gaps = local minima, shoulders = three consecutive inflection points, in model profiles from 2000 posterior samples

recipe.goal: Estimate optical depths and dust temperature
recipe.method: tau = -ln(1 - I/B(Td)) with irradiated-disk temperature Td
assumptions: Scattering neglected; flaring angle 0.02; stellar heating only

recipe.method: Integrate model intensity profile with cos i / d^2; R68 and R90 enclosing 68% and 90% flux
linmix regression of log R68 vs log Lmm (flux scaled to 140 pc), with flux, 10% calibration, and distance uncertainties sampled

recipe.goal: Assess dust trapping via ring width to scale height
recipe.method: Compute w_d/h_p for high-contrast rings (depth <0.5) with w_d = sigma_i
Zhang et al. 2018 scaling relations with gap width, Sigma_dust, St_max, h/r
key_parameters: kappa_abs = 0.43 cm^2/g, amax=0.1 mm, n(a)∝a^-3.5, alpha = 1e-3
assumptions: One planet per gap; DSHARP dust composition

answer_key.quantity: SO 1274 inner three gap period ratio

evidence.quote: close to a 3:2:1 period ratio (more precisely, 3.08:1.95:1)

not_stated_but_needed: Exact line-free/flagged channel ranges in archival data
Self-calibration solution intervals and which EBs/ cleaning parameters (niter, thresholds, masks, scales, cell, image size) were used
Prior means and standard deviations for the parametric model
Initial guesses for N rings and hyperparameters of the pyro guide beyond learning rate
Zenodo products must be downloaded to reproduce; CLEAN model used for weight rescaling not given
Distance values adopted for each target in the modeling (Table 1 values assumed)
missing_for_reproduction: Priors, CLEAN masks/thresholds and cell/image sizes
Analysis code not stated as released
score_reason: Public data and Zenodo products with clear model equations and tables, but priors, imaging parameters and code are not specified.
rediscovery_reason: Data are public (and reduced visibilities are released), model form is explicit, results are numeric tables.
